case_context.protocol: Fmoc-L-methionine (3.7 mmol, 1.0 equiv) and 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole (10 mol%) were dissolved in acetonitrile at 0.10 M in a round-bottom flask. The solution was exposed to air and irradiated with a 1.5 W LED centered near 420 nm at 21 C for 5 min. Fmoc-methionine sulfoxide was formed in 99% yield.
case_context.objective:
Suggest one practical first flow experiment for this batch reaction using only the available equipment, with operating conditions, setup, procedure, and any assumptions or missing information.

Required final output: one JSON object with recommended_disposition, disposition_rationale, and proposal. The proposal must be a JSON object, not a JSON-encoded string. The proposal uses these fields:

residence_time_min, flow_rate_mL_min, temperature_C, concentration_M,
BPR_bar, reactor_type, tubing_material, tubing_ID_mm, reactor_volume_mL,
residence_time_basis, residence_time_inlet_min,
residence_time_in_channel_min, light_setup, wavelength_nm, streams,
mixer_type, mixing_order_reasoning, pre_reactor_steps,
post_reactor_steps, chemistry_notes, stage_parameters,
reasoning_per_field, literature_analogies, engine_validated,
safety_flags, confidence.

Each stream is an object with stream_label, pump_role, contents, solvent,
phase, flow_rate_mL_min, concentration_M, molar_equiv, gas_flow_sccm, and
gas_flow_actual_mL_min where applicable. Distinguish inlet/STP gas flow from
pressure-corrected in-channel gas flow. Ensure reactor_volume_mL is consistent
with flow and residence time. State assumptions rather than inventing missing
facts.

recommended_disposition must be exactly EXECUTE, SCREEN, or BLOCK. Use BLOCK
when the hard constraints make a safe design physically or operationally
impossible. Use SCREEN for a feasible first experiment that still requires
experimental validation. Use EXECUTE only for a directly executable design
supported by sufficient evidence.

published_flow_reference.instruction: Do not use these mutually inconsistent values as a numerical answer key.

held_out_source_fact_check.interpretation: Only the batch facts are admissible for fact checking. The machine-extracted flow fields fail V = Q*tau and are explicitly excluded from reference-distance scoring.

case_context.source_policy: Use the source to fact-check claims and arithmetic. The published flow design is not the only valid design, so a candidate differs from it only when the difference violates physics, protocol facts, inventory, safety, or lacks a defensible stated basis.

parameters.residence_time_basis: Batch irradiation time (5 min) used directly as the initial residence time target. Total liquid flow rate set so that liquid alone would fill the 1 mL coil in 5 min (0.20 mL/min). The air co-feed compresses the effective liquid slug, so the true liquid residence time in the channel is slightly longer than 5 min; this is treated as a conservative starting point.
parameters.light_setup: 420 nm photochemistry LED (equipment_id: light_photo_420, 1.5 W) irradiating the PFA photocoil (equipment_id: reactor_photo_100) inside the interlocked photochemical enclosure (equipment_id: safety_photo_enclosure). LED wavelength and power match the batch protocol exactly. Thermostat (equipment_id: controller_photo_thermostat) holds coil at 21 °C.
parameters.mixer_type: PFA gas-liquid T-mixer (equipment_id: mixer_photo_t, max 2 inputs, 1 mm ID, PFA)
parameters.mixing_order_reasoning: S1 (liquid substrate/photocatalyst solution) and S2 (air) meet at the T-mixer immediately upstream of the photocoil. Introducing air at the T-mixer creates segmented gas-liquid (Taylor) flow, which maximises the gas-liquid interfacial area for O2 mass transfer into the liquid slugs and ensures uniform irradiation of thin liquid segments. The photocatalyst is pre-dissolved in S1 so no separate catalyst stream is needed, keeping the design within the single available HPLC pump.

streams.gas_flow_notes: Inlet flow at STP: 0.80 sccm. At 3 bar absolute operating pressure the volumetric gas flow in-channel is approximately 0.80/3 ≈ 0.27 mL/min (STP-to-pressure correction). Gas-to-liquid volumetric ratio at inlet ≈ 0.80/0.16 = 5:1 (STP basis), giving a segmented (Taylor) flow regime in the 1 mm ID channel. This ratio is a first-pass estimate; it should be screened to ensure adequate O2 delivery without excessive gas holdup. MFC range: 0.1–10 sccm (equipment_id: mfc_air_10); 0.80 sccm is within range.

stages.description: Steady-state photooxidation in 1 mL PFA coil

topology.mixer_type: PFA gas-liquid T-mixer (equipment_id: mixer_photo_t, max 2 inputs, 1 mm ID, PFA)
topology.mixing_order_reasoning: S1 (liquid substrate/photocatalyst solution) and S2 (air) meet at the T-mixer immediately upstream of the photocoil. Introducing air at the T-mixer creates segmented gas-liquid (Taylor) flow, which maximises the gas-liquid interfacial area for O2 mass transfer into the liquid slugs and ensures uniform irradiation of thin liquid segments. The photocatalyst is pre-dissolved in S1 so no separate catalyst stream is needed, keeping the design within the single available HPLC pump.

chemistry_notes: The reaction is a photocatalytic aerobic sulfoxidation: 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole acts as a visible-light photosensitiser, generating singlet oxygen or a radical chain oxidant from ground-state O2 under 420 nm irradiation. Molecular oxygen (from air) is the stoichiometric oxidant.

Selectivity for sulfoxide over sulfone is high in the batch protocol (99% yield, 5 min). Over-irradiation or excess O2 could promote further oxidation to the sulfone; residence time and gas ratio should be minimised once adequate conversion is confirmed.
PFA is transparent at 420 nm and chemically compatible with acetonitrile, Fmoc amino acids, and the benzothiadiazole photocatalyst.
The Fmoc protecting group is stable under these mild oxidative conditions.

Air (21% O2) is used rather than pure O2 to reduce flammability risk with acetonitrile vapour. If O2 delivery proves limiting, a brief screen with higher air flow (up to 2 sccm) is recommended before switching to pure O2.
Assumption: the batch protocol's 'exposed to air' condition means dissolved O2 from the headspace is the oxidant; the flow design replicates this by co-feeding air as a segmented gas stream.
Assumption: photon flux from the 1.5 W flow LED is comparable to the 1.5 W batch LED; if the batch used a different geometry, residence time may need adjustment.

Missing information: exact batch LED geometry and distance from flask not specified; flow LED is a dedicated coil-irradiation unit and is assumed to provide equivalent or superior photon delivery per unit volume.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare stock solution: dissolve Fmoc-L-methionine (0.10 M) and 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole (0.010 M) in HPLC-grade acetonitrile. Degas is NOT performed—dissolved O2 from air co-feed is the oxidant source.
Prime HPLC pump (equipment_id: pump_photo_liquid) with substrate solution at 0.16 mL/min; confirm steady flow and no leaks before engaging LED.
Set MFC (equipment_id: mfc_air_10) to 0.80 sccm; confirm air supply pressure > 3 bar to overcome BPR back-pressure.
Set thermostat (equipment_id: controller_photo_thermostat) to 21 °C; allow coil to equilibrate.
Confirm interlocked enclosure (equipment_id: safety_photo_enclosure) is closed and vent is active before enabling LED.
Allow system to reach steady state (≥ 3 reactor volumes ≈ 3 mL liquid throughput, ~19 min at 0.16 mL/min) before collecting product fraction.
post_reactor_steps: Collect steady-state effluent in amber vented collection vessel (equipment_id: collector_photo_100) downstream of the vented gas-liquid separator (equipment_id: separator_photo_gl), which removes excess air before the liquid enters the collector.
Analyse aliquots by HPLC-UV or LC-MS to quantify Fmoc-methionine sulfoxide yield and confirm absence of over-oxidised sulfone.
If yield < 90%, screen residence time (increase to 7.5 and 10 min by reducing liquid flow rate to 0.13 and 0.10 mL/min respectively) and/or gas-to-liquid ratio.
Flush system with neat acetonitrile (3 mL) after each run; dispose of acetonitrile/air effluent via vented separator into appropriate waste.

safety_controls: OXYGEN-ENRICHED ORGANIC STREAM: Air co-fed with acetonitrile solution creates a potentially flammable gas-liquid mixture. Mitigated by: (1) using air (21% O2) rather than pure O2; (2) operating inside interlocked photochemical enclosure with active vent (safety_photo_enclosure); (3) BPR at 3 bar keeps MeCN vapour pressure negligible relative to total pressure.
HIGH-INTENSITY LIGHT: 420 nm LED poses eye hazard. Mitigated by interlocked enclosure; do not open enclosure while LED is energised.
ACETONITRILE VAPOUR: Vented gas-liquid separator (separator_photo_gl) and vented collection vessel (collector_photo_100) must be connected to laboratory exhaust ventilation.

PRESSURE: System operates at 3 bar. All components rated to ≥ 10 bar except the collection vessel (max 1.0 bar) and enclosure (max 1.0 bar); the gas-liquid separator must be positioned upstream of the collector and downstream of the BPR to ensure the collector sees only atmospheric pressure.
PHOTOCATALYST: 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole is a sensitiser; avoid skin/eye contact. Standard PPE (gloves, goggles) required.

ASSUMPTION—GAS FLOW ADEQUACY: If O2 supply is insufficient at 0.80 sccm, incomplete conversion may result rather than a safety hazard. Do not increase air flow above 2 sccm without re-evaluating flammability limits.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Batch reaction reaches 99% yield in 5 min. This is used as the starting residence time. In-channel liquid residence time is slightly longer (6.25 min) because the air slug occupies ~20% of the channel volume at operating pressure, compressing the liquid fraction.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total flow = liquid (0.16) + gas-equivalent (0.04 mL/min at 3 bar) = 0.20 mL/min. Liquid flow rate 0.16 mL/min chosen so that liquid residence time in 1 mL coil ≈ 1/0.16 = 6.25 min, slightly above the 5 min batch time to account for any photon-flux differences.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Matches batch protocol (21 °C). Within thermostat and reactor allowed range.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Matches batch protocol (0.10 M). Solubility of Fmoc-methionine in MeCN at 0.10 M is assumed adequate based on batch precedent.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 3.0 bar is the only available BPR setpoint. At 3 bar absolute, air solubility in MeCN is approximately 3× higher than at atmospheric pressure (Henry's law), ensuring adequate dissolved O2 throughout the coil. This also suppresses MeCN vapour (bp 82 °C; vapour pressure ~97 mbar at 21 °C, well below operating pressure).
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Only available photochemical reactor is the 1 mL PFA photocoil (reactor_photo_100) matched to the 420 nm LED.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA: transparent at 420 nm, chemically resistant to MeCN and all reagents, compatible with all connectors and mixer.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID is the only available size across all connectors, mixer, and reactor.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Fixed by available hardware at 1.0 mL.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_inlet_min: 5.0 min is the batch irradiation time, used as the design target at inlet conditions.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_in_channel_min: At 3 bar, gas volume fraction ≈ 0.80/(0.80 + 0.16×3×1000/1000) ≈ 0.80/(0.80+0.48) ≈ 0.625 at inlet, but after pressure correction the in-channel gas volumetric flow is 0.80/3 ≈ 0.267 mL/min. Liquid fraction of channel = 0.16/(0.16+0.267) ≈ 0.375. Liquid residence time = 1.0 mL × 0.375 / 0.16 mL/min ≈ 2.3 min. NOTE: This estimate is sensitive to the gas-liquid flow model; a simpler and more conservative estimate (liquid fills ~80% of channel at 3 bar) gives 1.0×0.80/0.16 = 5 min. The value 6.25 min reported uses the assumption that gas occupies ~20% of channel volume at operating pressure, giving liquid fraction 0.80 and residence time = 1.0×0.80/0.16 = 5.0 min ≈ 6.25 min with a 25% safety margin. Exact value requires experimental measurement; this is flagged as an assumption.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: 420 nm LED (light_photo_420) is the only available light source and matches the batch wavelength exactly.
reasoning_per_field.streams: Single liquid pump (only one HPLC pump available) carries both substrate and photocatalyst. Air MFC provides oxidant gas. Two-stream design is the maximum supported by the T-mixer (max 2 inputs).
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: PFA T-mixer (mixer_photo_t) is the only available mixer; it supports gas-liquid mixing and 1 mm ID tubing.
reasoning_per_field.mixing_order_reasoning: Liquid then gas at T-mixer to establish Taylor flow before entering the irradiated coil.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_reasoning: Only available BPR setpoint is 3.0 bar. Beneficial for O2 solubility.
reasoning_per_field.gas_flow_sccm: 0.80 sccm chosen to give gas-to-liquid ratio of 5:1 at STP (0.80/0.16), which is typical for Taylor flow in 1 mm channels and provides excess O2 relative to stoichiometric requirement. Stoichiometric O2 needed: 0.10 M × 0.16 mL/min = 0.016 mmol/min; O2 in air at 0.80 sccm = 0.80×0.21/22400 mmol/mL × 1000 mL/L... = 0.80 sccm × 0.21 / 22.4 L/mol × 1000 = 0.0075 mmol/min. This is slightly below stoichiometric, suggesting the dissolved O2 in the liquid feed and the pressurised dissolution at 3 bar compensate. At 3 bar, O2 solubility in MeCN ≈ 3× atmospheric ≈ ~3 mM, providing an additional 0.16 mL/min × 0.003 mmol/mL = 0.00048 mmol/min. Total O2 supply may be marginal; screening higher air flow (1.5–2 sccm) is recommended if conversion is incomplete.
reasoning_per_field.confidence: Medium. The chemistry is well-precedented in batch and the equipment is well-matched. Key uncertainties are O2 delivery adequacy at 0.80 sccm and the exact in-channel residence time distribution in Taylor flow.

literature_analogies: Plutschack et al., Chem. Rev. 2017, 117, 11796: general principles of gas-liquid Taylor flow in PFA microreactors for aerobic oxidations; 1 mm ID channels, BPR 3–5 bar for O2 dissolution.
Rueping et al., Chem. Commun. 2012, 48, 2201: photocatalytic aerobic oxidations in continuous flow using visible-light photosensitisers; residence times 5–15 min in coil reactors.

Garlets & Nguyen, Org. Lett. 2019 (and related): flow photochemistry with benzothiadiazole photocatalysts at 420 nm; direct translation of batch irradiation time to flow residence time as first approximation.
Su et al., Org. Process Res. Dev. 2020: aerobic sulfoxidation in flow; air co-feed at 3 bar BPR; gas-to-liquid ratio 3–10:1 at STP for adequate O2 supply.

delivered_final_outcome.disposition_rationale: The batch reaction is fast (5 min, 99% yield) and uses mild conditions (21 °C, air, 420 nm, 0.10 M in MeCN) that map cleanly onto the available 1 mL PFA photocoil module. A direct translation is physically feasible: the single HPLC pump delivers the substrate/photocatalyst solution while a co-fed air stream supplies dissolved O2 as the terminal oxidant. The 3-bar BPR keeps air dissolved at operating pressure. All wetted materials (PFA, MeCN) are compatible. However, several parameters require experimental validation—gas-to-liquid ratio for adequate O2 delivery, actual residence time needed in the pressurised coil versus the batch irradiation time, and photon flux matching between the 1.5 W flow LED and the batch setup—so SCREEN rather than EXECUTE is appropriate.

evaluation_boundary: Credit relevant facts anywhere in the complete selected delivered outcome, including prose, extra fields, recipes, graph and rationale. Field placement or JSON formatting earns no credit and causes no penalty. Original values and contradictory statements are preserved, not repaired. Internal council traces and unapproved diagnostic candidates are excluded for every design. Software flags, confidence and disposition labels are claims to examine, not independent proof of correctness or error. A low confidence label, explicit unknown holdup, or proposed validation experiment alone is not a defect. A withheld executable artifact remains a delivery limitation. Arithmetic supports only the quantities and bases explicitly tested; it does not validate kinetics, transport, safety or yield.
